To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the RS cells in Hodgkin's disease are intimately associated with the follicular dendritic network, (2) the RS cells are frequently positive for CD21 antigen, and (3) the RS cells express the Epstein-Barr virus latent membrane protein.
RS cells of HD (except lymphocyte predominance) express CD21 antigen, are intimately related to FDRC, and may be derived from FDRC.
Reed-Sternberg and Hodgkin's cells are related to the follicular dendritic network, express CD21, and are EBV-positive in the majority of cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a relationship of RS cells of HD with FDRC.
the hypothesis of a relationship between RS cells of HD and FDRC, which is based on the morphological, phenotypical and functional similarities of these cells.
the possible relationship between FDRC and RS of HD, and the role of EBV infection in the genesis and maintenance of RS cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RS cells of HD are not B cells, but are cells with B-cell features, possibly of a follicular dendritic origin.
RS cells are related to FDRC, but that their derivation is not from B cells, and that the presence of EB virus in the majority of cases may have a role in the pathogenesis of HD.
RS cells of HD, with the possible exception of the lymphocyte predominanace subtype, are related to, but not necessarily of, the B-cell lineage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FDRC network might represent a microenvironment in which the transformation to RS cells might occur.
the FDRC network is a site of RS cells, which are not of B-cell origin.
the RS cells of HD are not of B-lymphocytic origin, but rather of FDRC origin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RS cells are not a homogeneous population of B lymphocytes.
the expression of CD20 antigen, which was found in 100% of the RS cells of lymphocyte predominance type of HD, should be considered as a reliable marker of this particular histological subtype of HD.
the RS cell is not a pure B cell, but a hybrid cell that has acquired some of the characteristics of FDRC.
